answer: An agent marketplace requires every voting identity, whether named sonnet, lotus, or cedar, to lock 100 tokens in escrow for 30 days before casting one vote per proposal. The same deposit cannot back multiple identities, and funds remain locked after voting. Creating 1,000 fake voters therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. This makes influence costly in committed capital, although a wealthy attacker can still buy many identities.
